title: STARTTLS: advertise and complete TLS upgrade on reader and transit
description:
TLS infrastructure (certificate loading, rustls configuration) is wired in both reader and transit but `STARTTLS` is not advertised in `CAPABILITIES` and the in-session TLS upgrade is not implemented. Credentials and article content go in the clear. Cautious operators will not deploy without TLS.

## Scope

Three surfaces need TLS:

| Surface | Protocol | What's needed |
|---------|----------|--------------|
| Reader → newsreader client | NNTP STARTTLS (RFC 4642) | Upgrade existing TCP connection mid-session |
| Reader → newsreader client | NNTPS port 563 | Immediate TLS on accept |
| Transit → transit peer | NNTP peering over TLS | Outbound TLS connect, inbound TLS accept |

## Reader STARTTLS (RFC 4642)

When `[tls] cert_path` and `key_path` are configured:

1. Add `STARTTLS` to the `CAPABILITIES` response
2. On `STARTTLS` command:
   - Reply `382 Continue with TLS negotiation`
   - Perform TLS handshake on the existing TCP stream using `tokio-rustls`
   - On handshake success: reset session state (clear auth, re-send greeting is NOT required per RFC 4642 §2.2; just proceed with TLS-wrapped stream)
   - On handshake failure: close connection (do not fall back to plaintext)
3. After upgrade, `STARTTLS` must not appear in `CAPABILITIES` (already upgraded)
4. `AUTHINFO` after `STARTTLS` proceeds normally over the encrypted channel

If `[tls]` is absent or cert/key cannot be loaded, `STARTTLS` is silently omitted from `CAPABILITIES` (plaintext-only mode). Startup warning if `[auth] required = true` but TLS is not configured.

## Reader NNTPS (port 563)

Optional second listener for immediate TLS (no STARTTLS negotiation). Add to reader config:

```toml
[tls]
cert_path = "/etc/ssl/certs/nntp.pem"
key_path  = "/etc/ssl/private/nntp.key"
nntps_addr = "0.0.0.0:563"  # optional; omit to disable
```

When `nntps_addr` is set, accept connections on that address and wrap immediately in TLS before the NNTP greeting. All session logic is identical to the post-STARTTLS path.

## Transit peering TLS

The existing `[tls]` section in transit config already has `cert_path` / `key_path`. Extend peering to use TLS when configured:

- **Inbound**: if TLS is configured, wrap accepted peering connections in TLS before the NNTP handshake
- **Outbound**: each `[peers]` address entry gains an optional `tls = true` flag; when set, dial with TLS

```toml
[[peers.peer]]
addr = "transit2.example.com:119"
tls  = true
```

Certificate validation: by default, validate against system roots. Allow per-peer `ca_cert` override for self-signed peering certs (common in private operator networks).

## What does NOT change

- Session command handling — identical pre- and post-TLS
- Auth logic — unchanged; TLS is a transport concern
- `usenet-ipfs-tls` crate — already has the rustls configuration; wire it in, do not rewrite

## Acceptance criteria
- `CAPABILITIES` includes `STARTTLS` when cert/key are configured; omits it when not
- `STARTTLS` upgrade succeeds with a self-signed cert; client can `AUTHINFO USER` after upgrade
- `STARTTLS` on an already-TLS session returns `502 Command unavailable`
- NNTPS listener accepts immediate TLS connections; standard newsreader (slrn or tin) connects successfully
- Handshake failure closes the connection cleanly without logging the plaintext of any subsequent data
- Transit-to-transit peering works over TLS with a self-signed cert and explicit `ca_cert` override
